reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Confusing Cognard type III with Borden type III (they are different definitions).
Omitting venous ectasia when distinguishing type III from IV.
name: Cognard Classification of Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas

version.label: Cognard revised classification (Cognard et al. 1995): I, IIa, IIb, IIa+b, III, IV, V
version.detail: Classified by venous drainage: sinus flow direction, cortical venous reflux, venous ectasia and spinal perimedullary drainage.

purpose: Classifies intracranial dural arteriovenous fistulas by venous drainage pattern, in more detail than Borden.
intendedPopulation: Patients with intracranial dural arteriovenous fistulas characterised by catheter angiography.

options.label: Type I: Drains into a dural sinus with antegrade flow
Type IIa: Drains into a sinus with retrograde flow in the sinus
Type IIb: Drains into a sinus with reflux into cortical veins; antegrade flow in the sinus
Type IIa+b: Drains into a sinus with retrograde flow in the sinus and reflux into cortical veins
Type III: Drains directly into cortical veins, without venous ectasia
Type IV: Drains directly into cortical veins, with venous ectasia
options.detail: Ectasia: draining vein over 5 mm and more than three times the diameter of the draining vein.

options.label: Type V: Drains into spinal perimedullary veins

resultStates.label: Type I
resultStates.summary: Drains into a dural sinus with antegrade flow.

resultStates.label: Type IIa
resultStates.summary: Drains into a sinus with retrograde flow in the sinus.

resultStates.label: Type IIb
resultStates.summary: Drains into a sinus with reflux into cortical veins; antegrade flow in the sinus.
resultStates.detail: Cortical venous drainage is associated with a higher risk of haemorrhage and neurological deficit. Management depends on symptoms, location and patient factors.

resultStates.label: Type IIa+b
resultStates.summary: Drains into a sinus with retrograde flow in the sinus and reflux into cortical veins.
resultStates.detail: Cortical venous drainage is associated with a higher risk of haemorrhage and neurological deficit. Management depends on symptoms, location and patient factors.

resultStates.label: Type III
resultStates.summary: Drains directly into cortical veins, without venous ectasia.
resultStates.detail: Cortical venous drainage is associated with a higher risk of haemorrhage and neurological deficit. Management depends on symptoms, location and patient factors.

resultStates.label: Type IV
resultStates.summary: Drains directly into cortical veins, with venous ectasia.
resultStates.detail: Cortical venous drainage is associated with a higher risk of haemorrhage and neurological deficit. Management depends on symptoms, location and patient factors.

resultStates.label: Type V
resultStates.detail: Associated with progressive myelopathy; assess spinal cord function according to the clinical situation.

clinicalContext.text: Classifies dural fistulas by sinus flow direction, cortical venous reflux, venous ectasia and spinal drainage.
Types IIb to V have cortical (or perimedullary) venous drainage, associated with more aggressive behaviour.

clinicalInsights.text: Cortical or perimedullary venous drainage present.
Spinal perimedullary drainage: examine for myelopathy.

limitations: Does not include symptoms, location or arterial supply.

guideSections.what: Seven types of intracranial dural fistula by venous drainage: I, IIa, IIb, IIa+b, III, IV and V.
guideSections.whenToUse: Detailed angiographic description of dural fistulas.
guideSections.howToPerform: On catheter angiography, identify the drainage route, the direction of sinus flow, any cortical venous reflux, venous ectasia and spinal perimedullary drainage. Assign the type.
guideSections.clinicalContext: An angiographic classification; management also depends on symptoms, location and patient factors.

sources.citation: Cognard C, Gobin YP, Pierot L, et al. Cerebral dural arteriovenous fistulas: clinical and angiographic correlation with a revised classification of venous drainage. Radiology. 1995;194(3):671-680.
